result.summary: The landlord said yes with no conditions in event 006 ("Yes please get that sorted"), so I recorded approval 45 as approved and moved the ticket to provider_selection. He doesn't need a reply. Ticket 87 (R/PM048-2) looks like a duplicate of this job, so I didn't assign a contractor here, to avoid sending two. I passed it to ops to confirm which ticket to keep and run the job on that one only.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord's approval in event 006 has no cost cap or conditions, and the classifier rated it 'approve' with 'auto'. So the landlord needs no reply and the approval can be recorded. Ticket 87 has the same property, created time and events 001-006, which points to a system duplicate. Assigning a contractor on both tickets could send two contractors to the same job, and ticket 86 has no contractor or tenant contact details anyway.

alternatives_considered.option: Assign a contractor on ticket 86 and notify the tenant
alternatives_considered.why_not: No contractor is on record for this ticket, there are no tenant contact details, and the identical ticket 87 means a likely double dispatch.
